title: implement minimal 1D conv (part 2)

atoms.evidence: ow = w - kw + 1 (minimal form, no stride/padding)
s_b, s_ic, s_w = x.stride() — explicit code comment warning 'Common error: xsWi is always 1, so if you put 1 here you won't spot your mistake until you try this with conv2d!'
x_strided = x.as_strided(size=(b, ic, ow, kw), stride=(s_b, s_ic, s_w, s_w)) — sliding kernel window across width
einops.einsum(x_strided, weights, 'b ic ow kw, oc ic kw -> b oc ow')
the whole exercise is windowing-then-einsum for 1D conv with batch + channels

the 'ic' label appears on both sides of the einsum spec ('b ic ow kw, oc ic kw -> b oc ow') so it is contracted — explicit teaching point in dropdown: 'in_channels - this is an extra dimension for weights AND for x, it IS summed over'
weights: Float[Tensor, 'out_channels in_channels kernel_width'] — the conv-kernel-shape atom for 1D (oc, ic, kw); proposed atom now confirmed at 1D too

atoms_in_seed_but_not_actually_present.reason: still a plain function (not nn.Module) — matches 0_2_17 pattern
